# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through these gestures. Mute can read the manual but can't speak or see the bomb. Mute is gesturing to me (Deaf), and I can see gestures but not hear speech.

Let me analyze the pattern: pairs of symbols, possibly encoding something like wire-number:action or condition:instruction pairs, since Mute knows the manual but not the bomb state, and I know the bomb state but not the manual.

The pairs: [👆🖐] [✌☝] [🤟👍] [👍☝] [✌🖐] [🤟✊]

This looks like it could be encoding (wire number, symbol) or (display value, action) pairs - Mute may be trying to establish a shared code before knowing my actual bomb state, or this is the manual's conditional logic being transmitted blind. Since Mute doesn't know my bomb state yet, this is likely a generic key/legend: mapping numbers or colors to symbols, waiting for me to respond with what I actually see.

I should respond with my actual bomb readings using gestures, since Mute can't hear me but also can't see - wait, Mute cannot see gestures either (Mute can only read manual, not see). So gesturing back to Mute is useless! I can only reach Mute via speech, and Blind via speech too. Let me check: my channels say "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." Gesture only reaches Mute per the channel list, but Mute cannot see... Actually the rules say gestures are only received by those who can see. Mute cannot see, so gestures to Mute do nothing.

I should speak instead, describing what I see, so both Mute and Blind receive it via speech.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ 👍 ☝]

Mute keeps gesturing to me, but as established, gestures to Mute don't work in reverse - but wait, I need to reconsider: Mute is gesturing TO me, and I CAN see gestures (I'm Deaf, meaning I can't hear but I can see). So I do receive these. The issue is only that MY gestures to Mute wouldn't be seen by Mute (Mute can't see). But Mute's gestures to me work fine since I can see.

So Mute is trying to tell me something via gestures repeatedly: [👍☝] and then [👍☝👍☝] (doubled). This might be Mute trying to signal "confirm" or asking me to repeat/acknowledge, or establishing a numeric code (like 👍=1, ☝=1, so "11" or "1,1").

Since I already spoke my bomb readings (display 0, light blue, wires green/yellow/red), Mute may not have received that yet due to turn order (Mute goes first, before Blind and me). My speech from Turn 1 would reach Mute at the start of the next round - so Mute should have received it by Turn 2's start. But Mute is still repeating the same gesture pattern, suggesting this is just Mute's fixed opening/protocol attempt that isn't a reaction to my info yet, or it's confirming receipt.

I can't decode this without more context. I'll continue relaying bomb state clearly via speech, and ask Blind (via speech) to relay back to me what Mute might be telling them if Mute now speaks. Actually Mute cannot speak at all. Mute can only gesture (to me) or... wait, Mute "cannot speak" per rules. So Mute's only channel is gestures to Deaf. That's very limited - Mute can only reach me, not Blind directly.

So the flow must be: Mute gestures to me (Deaf), I interpret and speak to Blind (and Mute, though Mute can't hear). This makes me the relay between Mute and Blind!

I'll acknowledge and try to establish a simple protocol. Since I don't know what the gestures mean yet, I'll ask Blind for the manual context via... I can't hear Blind either. I only speak, others receive. This is one-directional for me mostly.

I need Mute to establish a code. Let me try assuming gestures encode wire actions using numbers: 👍=1(yes/first), ☝=1. Perhaps it's "wire 1, cut" repeated for emphasis given my display is 0.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see display 0, light blue, wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute, I received your gestures but do not know your code yet. Please try distinct single symbols per wire number, one at a time, slowly.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

Mute is now sending a single repeated symbol: 🤟, three times. This could be Mute's response to my request for "distinct single symbols" - trying again with simpler signals. Since Mute can't hear me yet (my speech takes a round to arrive), this might not be a response to my request at all, but a continuation of their own sequence.

Given the timing: Speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. My speech from turn 2 would reach Mute at the *start* of turn 3's round - meaning Mute should have received it before acting in turn 3. So this repeated 🤟 might actually be Mute's reply to my request for simpler signals, giving me one symbol at a time, repeated for emphasis/confirmation that this is one distinct signal.

Let me think about what 🤟 could map to. If Mute is going through manual conditions based on my bomb state (display 0, light blue, wires 1-green 2-yellow 3-red), and sending me a single symbol repeatedly to confirm it's an important instruction, this could mean something like "wire 3" (matching red?) or a specific action symbol.

I don't have enough info yet. I should keep encouraging a numbering scheme and pass info to Blind too, since Blind needs to eventually act.

```
speak(text="Deaf here again, display still 0, light blue, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, I see you sending the same single gesture three times: love-you sign. If that means yes or wire one, gesture thumbs up once. If it means something else, try a different single symbol next.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Mute is now sending 👍 three times. This is likely a direct response to my last message where I said "gesture thumbs up once" if 🤟 meant "yes" or something specific. Mute sent it three times instead of once - possibly emphasizing agreement, or confirming three times because there are three wires, or simply affirming strongly.

Given the context, it seems plausible that 🤟 confirmed something, and now 👍👍👍 is a strong "yes" confirmation. But I still don't know what the original message was about specifically.

Let me try a more structured approach - I'll propose a clear numeric gesture code where Mute can answer yes/no questions about the bomb resolution using ☝✌🤟 for wire numbers 1/2/3, and 👍/👎 for yes/no, since Mute seems to be trying to communicate but we lack a shared protocol.

```
speak(text="Deaf here, bomb unchanged: display 0, light blue, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Mute, let's use a simple code. Gesture one finger symbol for wire one, two-finger for wire two, three-finger for wire three, to tell me which wire to cut. Then thumbs up if display or light matters, thumbs down if not.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Now Mute sends 🤟 followed by 👎. Following my proposed code: ☝ = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3 (three fingers). So 🤟 = wire 3! And 👎 = "no" to my question about whether display/light matters.

So this suggests: **Wire 3 is the one to cut**, and display/light don't matter (or the answer is "no" to whatever I asked - though my question was a bit ambiguous, "thumbs up if display or light matters, thumbs down if not").

This is great progress. Let me confirm this understanding with Mute and pass this critical info to Blind, who actually needs to act on the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I understand: three-finger sign means wire three, thumbs down means display and light do not matter. Confirming - is wire three the one to cut? If yes, thumbs up. If no, thumbs down.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf relaying from Mute via gesture code. Current signal indicates wire three may be the one to cut, and the display and light readings do not matter. Wire 3 is red. Wait for my confirmation before cutting anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirms with a single 👍 (thumbs up) - this confirms that wire three is the one to cut, per my confirmation question. 

This is a clean, unambiguous confirmation. Let me relay this final instruction to Blind clearly so they can act.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf here. Confirmed by Mute: cut wire three, which is red. Display and light do not matter. Proceed to cut wire 3.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here, relaying to Blind now: cut wire three. Thank you for confirming.")
wait()
```
